PROPOSAL (post-pilot, not now): ring the live collision flag through Claude Code's per-session inbox socket. Verified against code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging + /channels on 2026-08-08.

What is real: every CC session binds a per-user UDS inbox and exports the path as CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET to hooks and Bash "before any hook runs, including SessionStart". Our SessionStart shim (`sofar event session-start`) is a child of the session, so capturing the path into the session record is a ~1-line change to an existing surface. Posted messages run through the same inbound controls as peer messages.

Five constraints that shape the design:
1. NOT the sanctioned surface. The messaging doc routes external-event push to channels ("To push external events, such as CI results or chat messages, into a session, use channels"). Channels are research-preview, need Anthropic auth, Bun, a session restart with --channels, and during preview only Anthropic-allowlisted plugins may register — closed to us today. So the socket is the available path, chosen knowingly, on an undocumented wire format.
2. Own-child exemption vs. value are in TENSION. Unverified-origin posts are "treated like any other that asserts no permission class" — delivered to a prompting session, HELD for approval in a bypassPermissions one. Only the session's own child processes get the exemption, and on macOS only while the posting process is still running. But the socket's unique value is waking an IDLE session (an idle session runs no hooks, so has no live child). Candidate resolution, UNVERIFIED: SessionStart spawns a persistent per-session sofar child that stays alive and rings its own socket; must not double-fork or the ancestry check likely breaks. Test before designing on it.
3. Delivery costs the user a turn — "counts toward usage like a prompt you type". Edge-triggered on new overlap only; never level-triggered on file change.
4. Throttled: identical repeats dropped in a short window, 50 unread cap, 100 held cap. Self-suppression is a feature here, not a problem.
5. Availability is narrow AND anti-correlated with our audience: macOS/Linux only, v2.1.224+, not on Bedrock/GCP/Foundry, and OFF entirely when DISABLE_TELEMETRY / DO_NOT_TRACK / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC / DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK disable feature-flag evaluation. Local-first users who set DO_NOT_TRACK — our most aligned ones — have no doorbell.

DESIGN LAW if this is ever built: the socket is a strictly optional last inch. The shipped hook path (2.1's UserPromptSubmit conflict line) stays the mechanism, always; every other tool and every gated session still gets the warning at orientation. Nothing may become correct only when the doorbell rings. Failure is silent by design (a refusing session "shows no visible change").

SUPERSEDES the socket-posting shape in the prior note. Better architecture, same goal: sofar is the ADDRESSING layer, Claude is the transport. sofar never posts anything and never opens a socket.

Grounding (verified 2026-08-08): both collision surfaces already carry Claude Code session ids, because sofar adopts CC's session_id at start_session (hook JSON -> "pass this as session_id"). core/fold.ts: ParallelWriteback { session_id, tool, ended, next_action }; core/adjacency.ts openSessionFileConflicts -> FileConflict { path, sessions: string[] }. We already know WHO collided and that they are claude-code. We just never tell the model it can reach them.

The move: where 1.2's end_session result and 2.1's UserPromptSubmit conflict line name a colliding session, also name it as a reachable peer. Claude then decides whether to use its OWN SendMessage tool. This sidesteps every constraint in the prior note at once — no undocumented wire format, no own-child verification, no inbound-controls hold, no tokens spent by sofar, no new transport to maintain, and no violation of the zero-model-calls invariant (we hand over an address; we do not call anything).

Degradation is free: if messaging is absent (DO_NOT_TRACK, Windows, Bedrock, old version, denied tools) the address is simply omitted and the surface is exactly what ships today. That satisfies the design law in the prior note by construction rather than by discipline.

OPEN QUESTION, the only real one: mapping a CC session id -> the peer NAME that SendMessage addresses. /list-agents rows show a short identifier and working directory, not obviously the session id. Options to check: whether CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET's path encodes the session id (capturable per session at SessionStart, which is a child, so this is cheap to record); or whether ListAgents output can be matched on cwd + id prefix. Verify before designing further. If no mapping exists, the fallback still helps: tell the model the peer is a live claude-code session in this repo and let it resolve via ListAgents itself.
